original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

selector_method: Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
selected_method: Derive the rank-two replacement-interface condition for a two-center in-flight relay, then exhaust its fully charged two-tap realizations.
scope_change_reason: The selector method was counterexample-oriented, so the construction-focused replacement-interface method on the same card was selected. Live overlap found a completed one-restoration post-read study (Cycle 18, Discussion #1166 comment 18930632); this run therefore changed the object to simultaneous omissions at two reciprocal helper centers and a two-tap in-flight defect relay, which PR #1937 explicitly leaves outside its cross-center leaf-vector census. The result is a bounded obstruction for that new candidate mechanism.
actual_scope: On the pinned PR1062 11,500-ADD R439 word, enumerate the three reciprocal singleton first-read helper-center pairs (643,525), (648,526), (650,534) and all four cross-products of one terminal D restoration from each center. For each two-omission word, test whether at most two existing A source-tap edits at distinct gates, with total scalar ADD charge at most +1, can restore the full 661-column forward and reverse state maps. The donor inventory is deliberately relaxed to every register label, without frame restrictions. A positive candidate would still need frame legality, frame-path and paid-profile checks, the twisted helper contract, integer precision bounds, and full assembly pricing; no candidate exists even in the relaxed map-preserving domain.
bottleneck_link: A positive result would save at least one scalar ADD in the finite bit word; the selected construction remains complex-bound, and no supplier adoption or kappa change follows from this local scope. The bounded negative result removes this two-center relay family from the immediate construction search.
stop_rule: Exhaust all reciprocal singleton first-read pairs in this pinned word, every cross-product of one terminal restoration per center, and every one- or two-tap A edit with total tap charge at most +1. Stop after the exact residual-rank/support factorization and complete all-register action inventory; do not extend to three or more tap edits, nonreciprocal pairs, other words or supplier assembly in this cycle.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json records the four exact residuals and rank-two factorizations, 20 candidate ordered gate pairs, 40 interaction orientations and zero cost-admissible tap pairs. verify.py recomputes the full F2 maps, source action inventory, parent pins, known positive absorption control and wrong-source rejection control.
claim_status: No advance claim was posted before the bounded experiment. Report as FINDING/DONE and release scope in Discussion #1166, following autoresearch.md.

open_questions.question: Can three or more A tap edits or a nonreciprocal center pair produce a fully charged multi-center defect relay?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The current exact obstruction covers only two simultaneous D omissions at reciprocal singleton first-read pairs and at most two A tap edits; larger edit sets can create new intermediate defect vectors.
open_questions.first_step: Start from a fresh selector seed and a distinct construction scope; if continuing this line, derive the rank-three residual factorization and its fully charged A-tap budget before any wider search.
open_questions.blocked_by: No universal obstruction is proved for three or more tap edits, nonreciprocal centers, other pinned R439 words, or changes to B/C.
